correctness.rationale: For any fixed positive sample, G has exact plateau C=[1-phi_hat(u-1)]/2; ML makes C=0, MO makes C=(v-u)/(2(v-1)). This and compact support of R=G-C give both exact fixed-n limits. For iid IG(1,phi), four explicit tail basis functions have finite unweighted L2 second moments x, x^3/3, x/3, 1/(3x); exact algebra expresses R in their empirical averages with root-n consistent coefficients and zero population mean, proving n||R||_2^2=O_P(1). Cauchy-Schwarz therefore permits every deterministic a_n downarrow zero. The MO influence H=X^2-X^-1-3(1+1/phi)(X-1) has exactly variance 6/phi^3, yielding sqrt(n)C=>N(0,3/(2phi)), and both scaled chi-square limits; ML scaled limits vanish. The actual check.py passed 50 exact/symbolic/numerical assertions and a supplementary seeded 7,000 replicate simulation. Independent expert checking is not claimed.

value.rationale: The original paper compares and recommends MO-versus-ML CDF–Stein tests at fixed positive tuning, reporting apparent parameter insensitivity. At the natural opposite zero-weight boundary, the raw statistics behave qualitatively differently: generic MO unweighted divergence vs finite ML, and under the null the MO scaled limit is universally one chi-square component with explicit shape-dependent coefficient, for any vanishing tuning rate. This identifies a practically relevant calibration/regularization boundary and the sole moment-mismatch direction governing the MO tail, beyond a routine reparameterization.
